chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who dies apostatizing from the religion of Islam and has children, he said: 'His wealth is for his Muslim children.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the wealth of a Muslim who dies as an apostate if he has Muslim children?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies that apostasy does not sever familial inheritance ties, ensuring the deceased's wealth passes to his Muslim offspring. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the child's faith, rather than the father's, determines the validity of the inheritance share, distinguishing it from the forfeiture of the apostate's own share in other contexts.
